blocks.text:
# CI: daily auto-publish

`daily-publish.yml` is a thin orchestrator that runs the five publish
channels once a day as isolated **legs**: one leg failing never kills the
others, and every failure self-files a GitHub issue. It duplicates no build
logic — each leg dispatches an existing workflow via `gh workflow run` and
watches the run.

## Schedule and change detection

- Cron `17 5 * * *` (daily, 05:17 UTC), plus manual `workflow_dispatch`.
- Legs run only when `main` moved since the last **green** daily run
  (compared by head SHA). No movement → every leg skips → the run stays
  **green** (the #159 lesson: a no-op must never be red). A dispatch can
  override with `force: true`.
- One daily at a time (`concurrency: daily-publish`, queued, never
  cancelled).

## Legs

| Leg | Runs | Publishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TestFlight | `build-mobile.yml` (`ios_content=all`, `android_content=none`) | iOS IPA → TestFlight, distributed straight to the EXTERNAL group (`TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP` repo variable + Beta App Review contact variables — lanes fail loudly without them). Android stays excluded (standing owner decision). |
| pub.dev | in-job | **Verifier + recovery**, never publishes directly: pub.dev trusted publishing only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs, which a schedule/dispatch run can never be. When behind, it classifies first (gh-1192): a tag-publish still **executing** (tag-run queued/in-progress at any age, or not visible yet / tag not cut while the bump is fresh) is a neutral **skipped: release in flight** — no error, no issue; the next daily re-verifies. Past the grace windows the recovery path applies: re-run the failed ci.yml tag-publish run (a rerun keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims); unrecoverable states fail loudly → issue with a manual-publish instruction. |
| CLI + desktop | `build-macos.yml` (`create_release=true`) | macOS DMG/ZIP (signed + notarized), macOS CLI bundles, `fa-extension.zip` → GitHub Release. |
| Website | `pages.yml` | fa1.dev: landing + web demo + `/extension/` + `/outlook/` slice. |
| Outlook add-in | `office-addin.yml` | Acceptance suite (manifest validation, dart2js taskpane, Node + Playwright e2e). The fa1.dev `/outlook` deploy itself rides the Website leg — `pages.yml` assembles the same add-in into the Pages artifact. |

Manual, version-by-version: `release-appstore.yml` (workflow_dispatch) submits the
version's latest processed TestFlight build straight to App Store review (iOS and/or
macOS). Pre-flight fails before any mutation — version must exist (create it via
`store-metadata.yml`), a processed build must exist, an already-submitted version is a
green no-op — and `confirm` must repeat `version` exactly. Release-after-approval stays
a manual ASC click (`APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE` repo variable flips it).

`workflow_dispatch` input `legs` selects a single leg (`all` by default) —
the safe way to smoke one channel.

## Versioning

The scheme: `scripts/auto_release.sh` patch-bumps
`pubspec.yaml` and pushes the bump commit straight to protected `main` as the
fa-release-bot GitHub App (the ruleset's only bypass actor, gh-1172 — the
2026-09-29 release-PR stopgap is retired); the push fires the ci.yml
`release-tag` job, and the tag drives the `publish`/`binaries` jobs. Manual
`workflow_dispatch` runs are input-gated: `releaseDryRun: true` exercises the
whole pipeline without the push/tag (AC1), and `releaseDispatch: true` on
`refs/heads/main` is the real push — bare validation dispatches (the SM's
per-PR `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch>`) arm nothing. The daily:

- lets `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` derive their version
  themselves (`latest tag + 1` at the child's own dispatch moment). A tag
  pinned once in the orchestrator would race `auto_release.sh` — the daily
  could attach assets to a tag minted at a different commit than the built
  code. Self-derivation keeps tag and code consistent; the two children
  derive within minutes of each other and converge on the same tag
  (`gh release create` attaches to an existing tag rather than moving it);
- never publishes to pub.dev itself (see the pub.dev row above) — pub.dev
  movement stays 100% in the auto_release → ci.yml tag job path, with the
  daily as verifier and rerun-recovery;
- keeps NO daily-side wedge alarm for a tag that is never cut (#1368): the
  old 1h `tag_cut_grace` horizon false-alarmed «never triggered» on a

single-leg green dispatch never advances the baseline, so a partial smoke
can't make the next scheduled run skip the legs it never exercised.

green daily becomes the baseline at the bump's sha — the plan gate

pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev, keeping the re-verification
and the failed-run recovery alive on a quiet main. A failing `plan` job
(not just legs) files its own
`[daily-publish] plan leg failed` issue — nothing escapes the loop.

On a failing (or timed-out) leg the `report` job files an issue:

- title `[daily-publish] <leg> leg failed`, label `bug` + `daily-publish`,

Each run also writes a single job-summary table (leg → version → status →
links) and exits red itself when any leg failed.

      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false

    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —

      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0

          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.

coverage-gate:
    name: Coverage ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — coverage ratchet green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          # gh-1477: blobless full history — the ratchet reads coverage
          # metadata + base...head commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      # PRs pay the ratchet on CHANGED lines only (issue #177 wave 2): the
      # 80% bar applies to the diff; main/tags keep the full-suite ratchet.
      - name: Diff coverage ratchet (PR, changed lines >= 80%)
        if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/diff_coverage.py
          --lcov coverage/lcov.info
          --base ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          --head ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          --min 80

      - name: Full coverage ratchet (main/tags, lib/ >= 80%)
        if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: python3 scripts/check_coverage.py 80

  guards:
    name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:

blocks.text:
# the gate needs flutter on PATH, pinned to the same 3.47.x the
      # consuming build legs use (PR #1304 rework thread 8).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 1): warm the pub cache with the shared
      # bounded-retry action so tag_release.sh's own enforce-lockfile smoke
      # rides it — the smoke stays in the script (release_hygiene NG2/AC3
      # pins it) but is no longer the job's first resolution, so one
      # transient git-dep clone reset cannot abort the pre-tag gate on a
      # cold cache (the v1.0.516 build-macos exit-69 class, on the release
      # path).
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Cut annotated tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          # gh-1192 AC3: pin the tag to the bump commit the push event
          # carried. head_commit.id is frozen at event time; a default
          # checkout can land on a main that moved in the seconds between the
          # bump push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178
          # interloper that way). tag_release.sh validates the sha (exact
          # bump subject + matching pubspec version) before tagging and
          # refuses to tag a moving HEAD when nothing qualifies.
          BUMP_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
        run: bash scripts/tag_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    if: always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing push/tag run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate. quality-gate aggregates every leg (always()), so its
  # failure verdict covers the whole matrix — the fa#456 lesson on
  # transitive skips: this job keys on the aggregator's result directly.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi

Alternative within ci.yml: trigger release-tag off the SCHEDULE instead? The schedule already runs every 2h ('23 */2 *') and the release job (bump push) is one job; release-tag could be another job in the same scheduled run that checks for an untagged bump commit on main and tags it! Actually scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh already has logic about "tag not cut yet + fresh bump on main -> skip (release-tag pending)". The release_flow_race test describes a daily verifier that knows release-tag's gate runs after bump.

So: convert release-tag from a push-triggered job to a schedule+dispatch-triggered job that:
1. Fetches main, finds the latest commit.
2. If it's a chore(release) bump commit without a corresponding tag → cut the tag (tag_release.sh already validates "exact bump subject + matching pubspec version" and BUMP_SHA... it currently uses github.event.head_commit.id).

But this changes tag_release.sh's input contract — BUMP_SHA from push event won't exist on schedule. tag_release.sh "validates the sha (exact bump subject + matching pubspec version) before tagging and refuses to tag a moving HEAD when nothing qualifies" — it can resolve the bump commit itself from origin/main.

Hmm, this is getting deep. Risk: breaking the carefully pinned release flow. The blast radius of reworking release-tag is huge (release_hygiene_test, release_flow_race_test, ci_pub_get_retry_guard_test).

Alternative pragmatic approach: leave the `release` and `release-tag` jobs' `if` arms untouched (they key on push-to-main which simply never fires once the trigger is gone), and drop the main-push trigger. Then: schedule arm of `release` job still bumps+pushes; but nothing cuts the tag → release pipeline stalls. NOT acceptable.

OK here's another thought — what does the schedule arm's bump push do today? Push bump commit → push trigger → full CI on main → release-tag cuts tag. The intermediate full-CI gate on the bump commit is what we're removing (that's the point of the ticket — no post-merge main CI). The ticket explicitly accepts release flow changes only via tags. Since the tag run itself runs the FULL gate (quality-gate on tags arm — non-PR → everything affected → full gate) and publish/binaries wait on quality-gate... does the tag run's quality-gate run? Check: on tag push, all jobs run incl. quality-gate; publish gates on quality-gate success. So the release pipeline's quality gate effectively MOVES from the bump-push run to the tag run. If the tag run reds, publish is blocked — but the tag exists; daily-publish recovery reruns the failed tag-publish run. Fine.

So the minimal honest change preserving the release flow:
1. ci.yml: drop `push: branches: [main]`.
2. Move release-tag OUT of ci.yml into `.github/workflows/release-tag.yml` triggered on `push: branches: [main]` with job-level if on chore(release) message. A 2h scheduled full run is a backstop the owner explicitly declined ("No nightly cron replacement (owner explicitly chose pre-merge over nightly)").

Hmm. But changing the schedule semantics is a bigger release-flow surgery. Middle ground: keep the schedule trigger for release catch-up, but that's exactly what it is. I'll keep it — it's the release flow, and the ticket says release flows stay. The "no nightly" non-goal refers to replacing main CI with a nightly validation cron; the release catch-up schedule predates and serves publishing. I'll document this.

Actually wait, let me reconsider — maybe gate ALL jobs except `release`/`release-tag`-related ones on schedule? No. Keep scope tight. Keep schedule.

Tag runs are push events (excluded → good: a red tag run is a release failure, not a flake; daily-publish + ci-red-report handle those). But the workflow_dispatch ALSO fires for manual releaseDryRun dispatches on main... releaseDryRun runs the release pipeline dry — failures there aren't PR flakes. Rare; the dedup-by-distinct-SHA logic (≥2 SHAs) mostly covers. I'll filter event == 'workflow_dispatch' and note that PR validation dispatches are the SM's. Dedup by test name "per #1364 lessons": by_test keyed by (file, name) already. OK.

Also update flake-watch.yml header comment to say PR-dispatch runs.

`scripts/sm_merge_guard.py`:
- input: --repo, --sha (the pushed head), --subject (commit message), --json runs (or fetch via gh)
- logic:
  - skip if subject starts with 'chore(release):' (release-bot bump; the tag run gates it)
  - fetch recent ci.yml runs (last 24h, limit 100): find runs with headSha == pushed sha, event == 'workflow_dispatch', conclusion == 'success'
  - if found → OK (validated tree landed)
  - else → ALARM
- workflow `.github/workflows/sm-merge-guard.yml`: on push branches [main]; job runs the script; on alarm (exit 3?), file deduped issue labeled 'sm-guard' / comment. Exit codes: 0 ok, 0 skipped, 3 alarm-with-issue-filed.

Wait — but SM merges: are they fast-forward (same SHA as validated head) or merge commits (new SHA)? If the SM merges with a merge commit, head SHA of main ≠ validated PR head SHA, and the guard false-alarms on EVERY merge. The ticket says "update branch onto main → dispatch ci.yml on the updated head → merge only when green... The tree that lands in main is byte-identical to the validated tree". "byte-identical tree" suggests the merge preserves the tree; if it's a squash merge, new commit SHA with same tree. If FF merge, same SHA.

And for each successful dispatched run, gh api .../commits/{run.headSha} → tree.sha. That's 2 API calls per run... limit: fetch runs first, filter by comparing trees only for the most recent ~20 dispatch runs. Cheap enough (hourly? no — on every main push; pushes are SM merges, serialized, maybe dozens/day).

Alternative cheaper: compare headSha equality OR tree equality. Implement: for each recent workflow_dispatch ci.yml run with conclusion success, fetch its head commit tree; if any equals the pushed tree → OK.

Hmm, but actually let me not over-engineer: I can compute the pushed commit's tree sha from the local checkout (fetch-depth: 0), and for each candidate run use `gh api repos/$REPO/commits/$headSha --jq .tree.sha`. Cap candidate runs at, say, 30 most recent dispatch runs. Fine.

- chore(release) subject → skip
- dispatch success with matching tree → ok
- no matching run → alarm
- matching SHA but failed conclusion → alarm
- push-event run (tag) match → not ok (must be workflow_dispatch)
- multiple runs, one match → ok

# gh-1537: [GOAL] Retire post-merge main CI: move every gate into the SM pre-merge validation run

## Description

## Owner directive

Stop the duplicated CI: today `ci.yml` fires on `push: [main]` IN ADDITION to the SM's pre-merge validation of the rebased branch. Owner's call: **everything moves into the pre-merge run** (not nightly) — then there are no surprises at all, and we save wall time twice: no post-merge main run, and (together with #1522 tag-sourced versions) no release-bot CHANGELOG commits triggering main churn.

## Why post-merge main CI is redundant now

- The SM loop (#687) already does: update branch onto main → dispatch `ci.yml` on the updated head → merge only when green, single serialized queue. The tree that lands in main is byte-identical to the validated tree → merge skew is excluded by construction.
- The heavy gates are ALREADY whole-tree in the dispatched run (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd — they are not staged-scoped in CI), so nothing unique runs on main today except repetition.
- Flake/red-main intake ("CI red → issue", e.g. #1442, #1530) must be RETARGETED to PR-dispatch runs (precedent: the #1532 wrap-perf flake was caught and filed from a PR-branch run, not main).
- Release/tag flows (`push: tags v*`, release binaries) are unaffected — keep them.

## Acceptance

1. `ci.yml`: drop `push: branches: [main]` (keep `tags: ['v*']` + `workflow_dispatch`). Verify no other workflow/job keys off main-push ci runs (branch-protection required checks already match dispatched runs on PR heads — confirm none require a main-context check).
2. SM (machine-sm/factory-sm): confirm the pre-merge validation dispatch covers EVERY gate that main CI covered, incl. whole-tree crap4dart/coverage/jscpd and the app-crap-gate equivalent; if any gate was main-only, move it into the dispatched run.
3. Flake intake: repoint flake_watch / red-main triage to consume PR-dispatch runs (dedup by test name per #1364 lessons); main-run watching removed together with the trigger.
4. Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ updated to describe the single pre-merge gate; note the interaction with #1522 (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).
5. Risk guard, explicit: the invariant is "SM queue is strictly serialized and validates the exact tree being merged". Add a cheap assertion/alarm for its violation (e.g. SM refuses merge if main moved after validation started) instead of relying on nightly backstop.

## Non-goals

- No nightly cron replacement (owner explicitly chose pre-merge over nightly).
- Tags/release CI stays.

Refs: #687 (SM validate-right-before-merge design), #1522 (tag-sourced versions kill release-bot commits), discussion 2026-10-11.

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; runs in every SM validation dispatch — path-blind
#               under dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 idiom; the nightly macos leg
#               stays the main/tag backstop)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Reserve only —
      # ci.yml has no pull_request trigger (dispatch-only CI); the
      # flutter-app-exzone leg gates on the SM validation dispatch itself
      # (gh-1280 idiom) and consults this output only if a real
      # pull_request trigger ever lands.
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}

      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path

# gh-1199 AC6 — flake safety net. Hourly: scan the failed ci.yml gate runs
# of the last 24h; a test red in >=2 DISTINCT-SHA runs is a proven flake
# (the #1171 signature — one SHA flipping green/red is noise, one red run
# is a regression). The watcher files/updates a `flake`-labelled issue
# with the failing runs and opens a reviewable PR adding the file to
# scripts/test_quarantine.json, which the gate legs apply via
# scripts/apply_quarantine.py (the file leaves the deterministic gate
# until the fix PR lands; nightly keeps running it supervised).
name: Flake watch

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '41 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  watch:
    name: Detect proven flakes, file/refresh issues + quarantine PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: write # quarantine PR branch (gh auth setup-git)
      issues: write # flake tracker issues
      pull-requests: write # quarantine PRs
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # quarantine PR branches from origin/main
          # gh-1477: blobless — the watcher scripts read test metadata /
          # commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          filter: blob:none

      # The scheduled token reads GITHUB_TOKEN with the job permissions
      # above; gh auth setup-git lets the script push the branch.
      - name: Watch for proven flakes (gh-1199 AC6)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh auth setup-git
          python3 scripts/flake_watch.py \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --window-hours 24 \
            --push-quarantine \
            --checkout .

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Flake watcher (gh-1199 AC6): catch the NEXT #1171 before it parks PRs.

Scans the failed ci.yml Quality-gate runs of the last N hours; a test that
is RED in >=2 runs with DISTINCT head SHAs within the window is a proven
flake candidate (the #1171 signature: same SHA can flip green/red, so a
single SHA never proves anything — and one red run is just a regression).
For each candidate the watcher:

    1. creates a `flake`-labelled GitHub issue (or updates the existing
       one) carrying the failing run links, the distinct SHAs, and a
       ready-to-paste entry for scripts/test_quarantine.json;
    2. with --push-quarantine, opens (or updates) a PR adding that entry
       so the gate skips the file pending the fix — the list is checked
       in and reviewed in the fix PR (gh-1199 AC6).

Tests already in scripts/test_quarantine.json are reported but not
re-filed. The gate legs apply the skip via scripts/apply_quarantine.py.

Requires the `gh` CLI and a token with issues+contents+pull-requests
write (GITHUB_TOKEN from the flake-watch.yml schedule is enough).

Pure stdlib + gh. Exit 0 even when nothing to do; 2 on usage/gh errors.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
QUARANTINE_PATH = os.path.join(HERE, "test_quarantine.json")
FLAKE_LABEL = "flake"


def gh(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"gh {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
    return proc.stdout


def failed_runs(repo: str, window_hours: int) -> list:
    since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=window_hours)
    out = gh("run", "list", "--repo", repo, "--workflow", "ci.yml",
             "--json", "databaseId,headSha,createdAt,conclusion,event",
             "--limit", "100")
    runs = []
    for r in json.loads(out):
        if r.get("conclusion") != "failure":
            continue
        created = datetime.fromisoformat(
            r["createdAt"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if created < since:
            continue
        runs.append(r)
    return runs


def failing_tests(repo: str, run_id) -> list:
    """[(file, test_name)] that failed in this run's integration shards."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["gh", "run", "download", str(run_id), "--repo", repo,
             "--pattern", "junit-integration-shard-*", "--dir", tmp],
            capture_output=True, text=True)
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            print(f"::warning::run {run_id}: no junit artifacts "
                  f"({proc.stderr.strip()[:200]})", file=sys.stderr)
            return []
        failed = []
        for dirpath, _dirs, files in os.walk(tmp):
            for name in files:
                if not name.endswith(".xml"):
                    continue
                try:
                    tree = ET.parse(os.path.join(dirpath, name))
                except ET.ParseError:
                    continue
                for tc in tree.getroot().iter("testcase"):
                    if tc.find("failure") is None and \
                       tc.find("error") is None:
                        continue
                    failed.append((tc.get("classname", "?"),
                                   tc.get("name", "?")))
        return failed


def load_quarantined() -> set:
    try:
        with open(QUARANTINE_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return {e["file"] for e in json.load(f).get("quarantined", [])}
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        return set()


def quarantine_entry(file: str, test: str, issue_url: str,
                     shas: list, runs: list) -> str:
    today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
    return json.dumps({
        "file": file,
        "test": test,
        "issue": issue_url,
        "since": today,
        "runs": runs,
    }, indent=2)


def find_issue(repo: str, title_key: str):

        f"## Flake: `{test}`\n\n"
        f"**File**: `{file}`\n\n"
        f"Red in **{len(shas)} distinct-SHA** Quality-gate runs within "
        f"24h (gh-1199 AC6 signature) — a model's mood or a schedule "
        f"shift, not the PRs' code, is the only thing those SHAs share.\n\n"
        f"### Failing runs\n{links}\n\n"
        f"### Distinct SHAs\n" +

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): awf main is load-bearing and review-gated, so
    # pack fixes go live on merge with no re-pin ceremony (recently
    # shipped on main: #579 conflict-rework, #577/#578
    # mutexExcludeSelf-by-fact-of-holding, #576 review-machine-unlinked,
    # #573-#574 pack snapshots + registry env, #572 review-stale-verdict,
    # #571 dmtools self-heal, #570 SM budget 1→3, #569 rework fatality,
    # #568 mergeBot workspace/repository args, #566 pack-registry runner
    # overrides). Accepted trade-off: a mutable ref executes whatever
    # sits at the awf main head at run start. The ENGINE (dmtools-agents)
    # resolves from releases via vars — no factory_ref here. Flip in
    # lockstep with the other machine-loop stubs — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
  `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`.
- `dart test` green (integration-tagged excluded from test-core — issue
  #551: `test/integration/**` changes also run the `integration-mock` leg
  per-PR: no-key legs via `MockLlmServer`, `--exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,
  perf,pty`; child-agent-spawn PTY tests carry `pty` and stay in nightly
  (issue #553). Tag-only CI = llm smoke + publish + binaries; nightly keeps
  the full real-provider suite (pty-integration).
  **The Quality gate is deterministic-only (gh-1199): mock LLM everywhere,
  live models never.** Real-provider files carry
  `@Tags(['integration', 'llm'])` and run ONLY in the tag-only
  provider-smoke job and nightly with secrets — the per-PR integration
  shards exclude them at selection (`shard_files.py --exclude-tag llm`) AND
  at invocation (`--exclude-tags browser-ext,llm`), so a model's mood can
  never block a merge. The boundary is self-enforcing:
  `scripts/check_llm_tag_boundary.py` (static-gate step + pinned audit)
  fails any integration-tagged file that looks live without the `llm` tag;
  `test/scripts/shard_files_llm_boundary_test.dart` proves the shard
  selection stays live-free. Real-model verification belongs to the bench
  harnesses (terminal-bench / harbor / MLS-Bench) run under supervision,
  plus manual `dart test --tags "integration && llm"` for debugging — NO
  scheduled-or-gate live runs in the PR path. A proven flake (red in ≥2
  distinct-SHA gate runs within 24h) is quarantined via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json` (checked in, reviewed in the fix PR;
  `flake-watch.yml` files the issue and opens the PR) — the gate legs pipe
  their targets through `scripts/apply_quarantine.py`, while nightly
  KEEPS running the file to produce the un-quarantine repeat-run proof.
- `cd flutter_app && flutter test --exclude-tags integration` green

blocks.text:
# CI: daily auto-publish

`daily-publish.yml` is a thin orchestrator that runs the five publish
channels once a day as isolated **legs**: one leg failing never kills the
others, and every failure self-files a GitHub issue. It duplicates no build
logic — each leg dispatches an existing workflow via `gh workflow run` and
watches the run.

## Schedule and change detection

- Cron `17 5 * * *` (daily, 05:17 UTC), plus manual `workflow_dispatch`.
- Legs run only when `main` moved since the last **green** daily run
  (compared by head SHA). No movement → every leg skips → the run stays
  **green** (the #159 lesson: a no-op must never be red). A dispatch can
  override with `force: true`.
- One daily at a time (`concurrency: daily-publish`, queued, never
  cancelled).

## Legs

| Leg | Runs | Publishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TestFlight | `build-mobile.yml` (`ios_content=all`, `android_content=none`) | iOS IPA → TestFlight, distributed straight to the EXTERNAL group (`TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP` repo variable + Beta App Review contact variables — lanes fail loudly without them). Android stays excluded (standing owner decision). |
| pub.dev | in-job | **Verifier + recovery**, never publishes directly: pub.dev trusted publishing only accepts OIDC from tag-push runs, which a schedule/dispatch run can never be. When behind, it classifies first (gh-1192): a tag-publish still **executing** (tag-run queued/in-progress at any age, or not visible yet / tag not cut while the bump is fresh) is a neutral **skipped: release in flight** — no error, no issue; the next daily re-verifies. Past the grace windows the recovery path applies: re-run the failed ci.yml tag-publish run (a rerun keeps the original tag-push event/OIDC claims); unrecoverable states fail loudly → issue with a manual-publish instruction. |
| CLI + desktop | `build-macos.yml` (`create_release=true`) | macOS DMG/ZIP (signed + notarized), macOS CLI bundles, `fa-extension.zip` → GitHub Release. |
| Website | `pages.yml` | fa1.dev: landing + web demo + `/extension/` + `/outlook/` slice. |
| Outlook add-in | `office-addin.yml` | Acceptance suite (manifest validation, dart2js taskpane, Node + Playwright e2e). The fa1.dev `/outlook` deploy itself rides the Website leg — `pages.yml` assembles the same add-in into the Pages artifact. |

Manual, version-by-version: `release-appstore.yml` (workflow_dispatch) submits the
version's latest processed TestFlight build straight to App Store review (iOS and/or
macOS). Pre-flight fails before any mutation — version must exist (create it via
`store-metadata.yml`), a processed build must exist, an already-submitted version is a
green no-op — and `confirm` must repeat `version` exactly. Release-after-approval stays
a manual ASC click (`APP_STORE_AUTOMATIC_RELEASE` repo variable flips it).

`workflow_dispatch` input `legs` selects a single leg (`all` by default) —
the safe way to smoke one channel.

## Versioning

The scheme: `scripts/auto_release.sh` patch-bumps
`pubspec.yaml` and pushes the bump commit straight to protected `main` as the
fa-release-bot GitHub App (the ruleset's only bypass actor, gh-1172 — the
2026-09-29 release-PR stopgap is retired); the push fires the ci.yml
`release-tag` job, and the tag drives the `publish`/`binaries` jobs. Manual
`workflow_dispatch` runs are input-gated: `releaseDryRun: true` exercises the
whole pipeline without the push/tag (AC1), and `releaseDispatch: true` on
`refs/heads/main` is the real push — bare validation dispatches (the SM's
per-PR `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch>`) arm nothing. The daily:

- lets `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` derive their version
  themselves (`latest tag + 1` at the child's own dispatch moment). A tag
  pinned once in the orchestrator would race `auto_release.sh` — the daily
  could attach assets to a tag minted at a different commit than the built
  code. Self-derivation keeps tag and code consistent; the two children
  derive within minutes of each other and converge on the same tag
  (`gh release create` attaches to an existing tag rather than moving it);
- never publishes to pub.dev itself (see the pub.dev row above) — pub.dev
  movement stays 100% in the auto_release → ci.yml tag job path, with the
  daily as verifier and rerun-recovery;
- keeps NO daily-side wedge alarm for a tag that is never cut (#1368): the
  old 1h `tag_cut_grace` horizon false-alarmed «never triggered» on a
  10.5h-old bump that self-healed 3 minutes later, so an untagged bump now
  reads `release-in-flight` ⏭️ in the daily for as long as it takes. The
  remaining tripwires for a genuinely stuck release: `auto_release.sh`'s
  one-time «pushed but untagged … proceeding so the next range absorbs it»
  log, the plan job's release-unresolved re-arm (every daily re-verifies
  while pub.dev is behind), and the tag-run selector in
  `scripts/verify_pubdev_release.sh`, which alarms `only non-push run(s)`

**Change baseline**: legs run only when `main` moved since the last green
daily **that ran all legs** (schedule runs, or `legs=all` dispatches). A
single-leg green dispatch never advances the baseline, so a partial smoke
can't make the next scheduled run skip the legs it never exercised.
One exception (gh-1192): a release-in-flight pubdev leg exits 0, so that
green daily becomes the baseline at the bump's sha — the plan gate
(`scripts/daily_plan.sh`) therefore still forces the legs while main's
pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev, keeping the re-verification
and the failed-run recovery alive on a quiet main. A failing `plan` job
(not just legs) files its own
`[daily-publish] plan leg failed` issue — nothing escapes the loop.

## Self-healing issues

On a failing (or timed-out) leg the `report` job files an issue:

- title `[daily-publish] <leg> leg failed`, label `bug` + `daily-publish`,
  assigned to `vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit`;
- body: daily run link, leg run link, failing job/step names, the last ~50

- **dedup**: an open issue with the same signature gets a comment instead
  of a duplicate;
- **auto-close**: when the leg goes green in a later daily run, the open
  issue is closed with a comment.

Each run also writes a single job-summary table (leg → version → status →
links) and exits red itself when any leg failed.

    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a

    # auto_release.sh with the bypass App's push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);

      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true))

      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # Defense in depth (gh-1172 round-3 BLOCK): the push rides the checkout
    # App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs write —

    # own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in the run.

      # expires with the job, never shared with other workflows.
      # NEVER minted on a dry-run dispatch: that arm fires on ANY ref, so the
      # bypass credential must not exist in a run that executes the (possibly
      # untrusted) dispatched ref's auto_release.sh — "dry-run never pushes"
      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (push, schedule, releaseDispatch) see a non-true releaseDryRun

      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0

        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true

          # bypass actor, so scope the token to what the push needs instead
          # of every permission the installation carries.
          permissions: contents:write

coverage-gate:
    name: Coverage ratchet
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — coverage ratchet green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          # gh-1477: blobless full history — the ratchet reads coverage
          # metadata + base...head commit ranges, never historical blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      # PRs pay the ratchet on CHANGED lines only (issue #177 wave 2): the
      # 80% bar applies to the diff; main/tags keep the full-suite ratchet.
      - name: Diff coverage ratchet (PR, changed lines >= 80%)
        if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/diff_coverage.py
          --lcov coverage/lcov.info
          --base ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          --head ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          --min 80

      - name: Full coverage ratchet (main/tags, lib/ >= 80%)
        if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: python3 scripts/check_coverage.py 80

  guards:
    name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

# the gate needs flutter on PATH, pinned to the same 3.47.x the
      # consuming build legs use (PR #1304 rework thread 8).
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 1): warm the pub cache with the shared
      # bounded-retry action so tag_release.sh's own enforce-lockfile smoke
      # rides it — the smoke stays in the script (release_hygiene NG2/AC3
      # pins it) but is no longer the job's first resolution, so one
      # transient git-dep clone reset cannot abort the pre-tag gate on a
      # cold cache (the v1.0.516 build-macos exit-69 class, on the release
      # path).
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      - name: Cut annotated tag + GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          # gh-1192 AC3: pin the tag to the bump commit the push event
          # carried. head_commit.id is frozen at event time; a default
          # checkout can land on a main that moved in the seconds between the
          # bump push and this job starting (v1.0.498 captured the #1178
          # interloper that way). tag_release.sh validates the sha (exact
          # bump subject + matching pubspec version) before tagging and
          # refuses to tag a moving HEAD when nothing qualifies.
          BUMP_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
        run: bash scripts/tag_release.sh

  # PR-gate twin of the release `binaries` job: the CLI bundle must compile
  # on every supported platform and actually run (`fa --help`) BEFORE a PR
  # can merge — but only when the CLI surface could have changed (issue
  # #177: a docs/app PR must not pay for five platform builds).
  #
  # gh-1280: merge-blocking validations ride `workflow_dispatch` (Machine SM
  # dispatches this workflow on the PR head; the dispatched run registers its
  # check runs on the head SHA), while this gate fired only on `pull_request`
  # events. Every real validation run therefore skipped the matrix and the
  # required "Binaries smoke gate" context went green-by-skip — a broken arch
  # build (the v1.0.512 linux/arm64 class) could never block a merge. On a
  # dispatched run the classifier treats everything as affected (non-PR
  # filter arm), so the full matrix runs exactly when validation is due;
  # docs-only pull_request runs keep the #177 path skip.

  binaries-pr:
    name: Binaries (PR)
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    needs: changes
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') &&
      (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - name: Pub cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Build CLI bundle
        shell: bash
        run: |
          # Same bundle layout as the release job: bundle/bin/fa (+ lib/).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output=build/out
          if [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ]; then
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah.exe build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe
          else
            mv build/out/bundle/bin/fah build/out/bundle/bin/fa
            chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          fi
          echo "$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary (macOS)
        if: matrix.os == 'macos'
        shell: bash
        run: codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      - name: Smoke — the binary runs (fa --help)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa"
          [ "${{ matrix.os }}" = "windows" ] && bin="build/out/bundle/bin/fa.exe"
          out=$("$bin" --help)
          echo "$out"
          [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "fa --help produced no output"; exit 1; }

  # Aggregation job so branch protection can require ONE stable context
  # ("Binaries smoke gate") instead of five matrix-leg names.
  binaries-smoke-gate:
    name: Binaries smoke gate
    needs: binaries-pr
    # gh-1280: same event fix as binaries-pr — on the SM validation
    # dispatches this aggregate must RUN (and carry a real conclusion),
    # never satisfy the required context by skipping.
    if: always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: All platforms built and smoked
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result == 'success' || needs.binaries-pr.result == 'skipped'
        run: echo "binaries-pr = ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
      - name: Fail the gate
        if: needs.binaries-pr.result != 'success' && needs.binaries-pr.result != 'skipped'
        run: |
          echo "binaries-pr result: ${{ needs.binaries-pr.result }}"
          exit 1

  # Every failing push/tag run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR failures are visible on
  # the PR itself, but main/tag reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate. quality-gate aggregates every leg (always()), so its
  # failure verdict covers the whole matrix — the fa#456 lesson on
  # transitive skips: this job keys on the aggregator's result directly.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."

# gh-1537: [GOAL] Retire post-merge main CI: move every gate into the SM pre-merge validation run

## Description

## Owner directive

Stop the duplicated CI: today `ci.yml` fires on `push: [main]` IN ADDITION to the SM's pre-merge validation of the rebased branch. Owner's call: **everything moves into the pre-merge run** (not nightly) — then there are no surprises at all, and we save wall time twice: no post-merge main run, and (together with #1522 tag-sourced versions) no release-bot CHANGELOG commits triggering main churn.

## Why post-merge main CI is redundant now

- The SM loop (#687) already does: update branch onto main → dispatch `ci.yml` on the updated head → merge only when green, single serialized queue. The tree that lands in main is byte-identical to the validated tree → merge skew is excluded by construction.
- The heavy gates are ALREADY whole-tree in the dispatched run (crap4dart baseline, coverage ratchet, jscpd — they are not staged-scoped in CI), so nothing unique runs on main today except repetition.
- Flake/red-main intake ("CI red → issue", e.g. #1442, #1530) must be RETARGETED to PR-dispatch runs (precedent: the #1532 wrap-perf flake was caught and filed from a PR-branch run, not main).
- Release/tag flows (`push: tags v*`, release binaries) are unaffected — keep them.

## Acceptance

1. `ci.yml`: drop `push: branches: [main]` (keep `tags: ['v*']` + `workflow_dispatch`). Verify no other workflow/job keys off main-push ci runs (branch-protection required checks already match dispatched runs on PR heads — confirm none require a main-context check).
2. SM (machine-sm/factory-sm): confirm the pre-merge validation dispatch covers EVERY gate that main CI covered, incl. whole-tree crap4dart/coverage/jscpd and the app-crap-gate equivalent; if any gate was main-only, move it into the dispatched run.
3. Flake intake: repoint flake_watch / red-main triage to consume PR-dispatch runs (dedup by test name per #1364 lessons); main-run watching removed together with the trigger.
4. Docs: AGENTS.md quality-gates section + docs/ updated to describe the single pre-merge gate; note the interaction with #1522 (fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn).
5. Risk guard, explicit: the invariant is "SM queue is strictly serialized and validates the exact tree being merged". Add a cheap assertion/alarm for its violation (e.g. SM refuses merge if main moved after validation started) instead of relying on nightly backstop.

## Non-goals

- No nightly cron replacement (owner explicitly chose pre-merge over nightly).
- Tags/release CI stays.

Refs: #687 (SM validate-right-before-merge design), #1522 (tag-sourced versions kill release-bot commits), discussion 2026-10-11.

# Runner split (gh-1005, 2026-09-30): pure-Dart AND all PTY/terminal jobs ->
# ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo: free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64
# queue). Flutter-test legs on arm64 bootstrap the SDK via git clone — Flutter
# ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable manifest is x64 only;
# subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64'); x64
# Flutter jobs keep the action. The self-hosted M5 pool is ONE runner
# (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent) reserved for genuinely macOS-only work:
# cube-kernel-live. PR PTY legs (integration shards, coverage/duration gates,
# Terminal visual) run hosted-Linux only and never wait on fa-m5-1.
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      releaseDryRun:
        description: 'gh-1172: run the release pipeline without the push/tag (logs the commit+tag that WOULD land)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (bump push + tag) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   flutter-app-exzone → JS-engine exclusion-zone tests on macOS (issue
#               #1267 N1; runs in every SM validation dispatch — path-blind
#               under dispatch-only CI, gh-1280 idiom; the nightly macos leg
#               stays the main/tag backstop)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (gh-1241 REG-1): a trajectory/session/usage-touching diff
      # runs the usage-fold suite per-merge.
      usagefold: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.usagefold }}
      # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Reserve only —
      # ci.yml has no pull_request trigger (dispatch-only CI); the
      # flutter-app-exzone leg gates on the SM validation dispatch itself
      # (gh-1280 idiom) and consults this output only if a real
      # pull_request trigger ever lands.
      exzone: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.exzone }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:

          # lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches.
          filter: blob:none
